pages.text: Every metal makes the full set, tools and armour, in the usual shapes. Each repairs with its own ingot and takes armour trims. Which to carry:$(br2)$(li)$(bold)Tin:$() early and soft; stone-grade mining, a step up from copper.$(li)$(bold)Lead:$() heavy. Iron-grade, slow swing, hits harder; the armour shrugs off knockback.

$(li)$(bold)Silver:$() soft but very enchantable; its tools and weapons do half again as much to the undead.$(li)$(bold)Nickel:$() iron that lasts longer.$(li)$(bold)Aluminum:$() light and fast, wears quickly, enchants well.$(li)$(bold)Electrum:$() the fastest tools and the best enchanting; fragile.

$(li)$(bold)Constantan:$() the workhorse, between iron and steel.$(li)$(bold)Invar:$() hard-wearing, the longest life short of platinum; the armour has a little toughness.$(li)$(bold)Platinum:$() diamond-grade mining, close to diamond's life, and it enchants better than diamond.
Vanilla's shapes, ingots and sticks. Silver for graveyards, lead for the gate.
Armour likewise. Only lead resists knockback; platinum is nearest diamond.

Ironworks adds copper, bronze, brass and steel sets on top; Spartan Weaponry makes its daggers, spears, longbows and the rest of all these metals too.$(br2)Alloys ($(l:patchouli:ore/metals)What the Metals Are For$()) mix in a heated basin: electrum, constantan and invar are made, not mined.
